fixed_during_audit: preview-host: session request filter used a raw URL prefix check

A percent-encoded escape (..%2F) in a subresource URL passes a raw startsWith check while resolving outside the output directory after decoding. Fixed: the filter now decodes (fileURLToPath), resolves dot segments (path.resolve) and compares against the resolved root; any parse failure fails closed (cancel).
main window had no navigation/window-open/permission guards

The renderer is local and CSP-restricted, so reachability was unproven (hardening note per anchors) — hardened anyway: will-navigate blocked for non-file URLs, window.open denied, permission requests denied by default.
The preload only uses contextBridge + ipcRenderer (both available to sandboxed preloads), so the full Chromium sandbox can stay on. Flipped to sandbox:true.
unknown invoke command types fell out of the switch
An unrecognized command.type returned an undefined response shape. Fixed: default case returns {ok:false, error:"unknown command: …"}.
hardening_notes: No auto-updater is configured: there is no update feed to attack, but release hardening (code signing, asar integrity, Electron fuses: runAsNode/nodeCliInspect off) must be added before any packaged distribution.
The renderer loads only local files and the CSP blocks remote scripts; keep it that way — remote content must only ever appear inside the sandboxed preview.
IPC payloads are trusted from our own renderer today; if the renderer ever renders attacker-supplied text into command payloads, add schema validation (zod/ajv) at the ipc.ts boundary.
